A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MindDrive and provide readable main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Corresponding material can be matched despite extensive reformatting and supplementary-section renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original Bench2Drive evaluations, IL-versus-RL comparisons, ablations and qualitative driving results, including appendix experiments.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds a 3B configuration, runtime measurements, route-level comparisons and further sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: The dual-LoRA experts, trajectory decoder and IL-to-PPO pipeline remain. Section 3.3 revises the stated losses: the PPO surrogate gains a minus sign, and the critic target becomes the explicitly defined return, advantage plus value, replacing v3's G_t target. These are limited objective-formulation changes; the PDFs do not establish corresponding implementation changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use Bench2Drive/CARLA, Chat-B2D and the same planning-QA driving coverage. The larger model, open-loop scores and added analyses remain within existing datasets and driving scenarios; no new domain or test environment is introduced.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds PGS, UniDrive-WM, MindDriver and AutoVLA, substantially strengthening the IL and offline-RL comparison set. AutoVLA was cited but not tabulated in v3. Existing comparators remain, and v4 additionally compares runtime against ORION and RecogDrive.

E3.justification: v4 adds Qwen2.5-3B experiments, an average-L2 metric over two seconds at 2 Hz, and runtime evaluation on an A100. It removes v3's ten-training-epoch statement and describes two online-RL epochs, relabeling the unchanged Figure 4 sweep from rollout rounds to training epochs. Seven reported rollout-route IDs also differ between v3 Figure A3 and v4 Table 4. These reported protocol revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v4 adds route-skill coverage analysis, runtime decomposition, individual-route IL/RL comparisons and a GAE trace-decay ablation in Tables 5, 7, 9 and 10. Table 11 extends the existing training-duration analysis with ability-specific results. The single-expert demonstrations and aggregate rollout-versus-other-route comparison are retained, not newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed variability, confidence intervals or statistical significance tests. Five rollout collections per route are described in both appendices. The added mean-runtime results introduce no uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: The original 0.5B results remain 78.04 DS and 55.09% SR. New results include MindDrive-L at 80.59 DS and 58.26% SR, open-loop errors, approximately 540 ms inference time, per-route scores and additional sensitivity results. The 3B scores concern an added configuration, not an improvement of the retained 0.5B result. Figure 5 also changes the first RL speed-action label from maintaining slow speed to speeding up.

T1.justification: v4 introduces the explicit return definition and repairs the PPO/value-loss formulation in Section 3.3. Appendix C adds piecewise speed and acceleration definitions. Equation 18 has an internal sign inconsistency: its deceleration branches require both negative speed change and a positive ratio defined from that change. No new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central contribution and first-online-RL-for-driving-VLA claim remain. The empirical headline broadens from the lightweight model's advantage over same-scale IL to MindDrive-L's claimed leading performance against newer IL and offline-RL methods, with 80.59 DS and 58.26% SR emphasized in the introduction.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive explanations for its open-loop disadvantage against DriveMoE, effective learning from sparse binary outcomes, the benefit of lambda equal to one, and performance regressions on individual routes. It also expands the rationale for separating the experts. The existing CARLA-only evaluation and simulator-synchronization limitations remain.

D1.justification: v4 adds Algorithm 1, annotation thresholds and ground-truth path-label instructions, route-to-scenario/skill mappings, trainable-parameter information and runtime hardware details. However, its appendix describes rule-based filtering while Section 3.2 still says manual filtering. v3's QT-former identification and Appendix E dataset-access/license statement disappear. The additions substantially change reproducibility documentation without proving corresponding implementation changes.

R1.justification: v4 updates citations and discussion with works including DrivePI, OmniDrive-R1, HERMES++, pi0.6 and ChatVLA. Appendix B makes the distinctions from ORION and the pi-series approaches more explicit. Raw2Drive is reclassified from offline to online RL. These updates refine the existing research positioning rather than redefine it.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the methodological narrative remain. v4 polishes wording, clarifies terminology, reorders ablation discussions and reorganizes supplementary explanations into an overview and questions section. Author, correspondence and acknowledgment text also change.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column to a single-column layout, with widespread figure resizing and relocation. Figure 1 is redrawn horizontally; Tables 3 and 4 become Table 3(a,b); the route-ID graphic becomes an expanded table; and several analytical tables are added. Figure 4's axis changes from rollout rounds to training epochs. Some expanded tables use substantially smaller text.

improvement.justification: The larger-model comparisons, measured runtime and route-level/sensitivity analyses strengthen evidence for scalability, efficiency and behavioral tradeoffs. Corrected PPO/value-loss reporting and pseudocode also help readers understand the procedure. These gains are tempered by unexplained changes in training descriptions and inconsistent annotation documentation, especially Equation 18's impossible deceleration conditions. The evidence supports a limited net improvement, with reproducibility issues remaining.
